name: Tien Gow
description: Tien Gow (Heaven Nine) is the oldest and most prestigious Chinese domino game. It is a trick-taking game played with a single set of 32 Chinese domino tiles. Players lead tricks with single tiles, pairs, triples, or quadruplets, and others must follow with higher-ranking tiles of the same group (Civil or Military). It is a game of deep tactical complexity and cultural heritage.

content.text: Tien Gow (Heaven Nine) is the oldest and most prestigious Chinese domino game. It is a trick-taking game played with a single set of 32 Chinese domino tiles. Players lead tricks with single tiles, pairs, triples, or quadruplets, and others must follow with higher-ranking tiles of the same group (Civil or Military). It is a game of deep tactical complexity and cultural heritage.

Tien Gow dates back to the Song Dynasty and is the ancestor of many modern tile and card games. It uses the standard 32-tile Chinese domino set, which represents all possible outcomes of two six-sided dice.
4 players, each playing for themselves (no partnerships).
Full set of 32 Chinese dominoes. No wild cards.
32 tiles (traditionally wood or bone), 4 dice (to determine dealer/seat), and score markers.
The 32 tiles are shuffled face down. Each player receives 8 tiles, usually dealt in batches of 4 (wood stacks).

items.text: Small Set Tien Gow: A faster version using only a subset of tiles or played with lower point stakes.
Macau Style: Specific house rules for scoring bonuses and 'doubling' the final trick value.
